item.text: The panel listener starts after `feed.start()`, so it misses a synchronous cached packet. Telemetry uses the same start order deliberately to count live deltas only. I’ll change the panel watcher and keep progress history separate from the display ordering check.

// The source is shared by visits of the same file. Decoding may settle later.
export function watchTransferProgress(feed, receive, record) {
  let nextFrame = 0;
  let displayedFrame = 0;
  const listener = event => {
    const frameNumber = ++nextFrame;
    const deliver = frame => {
      record(frame);
      if (frameNumber > displayedFrame) {
        displayedFrame = frameNumber;
        receive(frame);
      }
    };
    const decoded = feed.decode(event.detail);
    if (decoded && typeof decoded.then === "function") decoded.then(deliver);
    else deliver(decoded);
  };
  feed.target.addEventListener("progress", listener);
  feed.start();
  return () => feed.target.removeEventListener("progress", listener);
}

item.text: The first check confirms the panel receives the cached frame. Its telemetry assertion was too broad: a diagnostic listener already attached to the shared feed also sees the panel’s later `start()` event. I’ll test telemetry’s own startup separately and rerun the ordering checks.

Updated [src/progress.js](/workspace/src/progress.js) so the panel listens before a warm feed emits its initial packet. It now records every decoded frame while preventing an older frame that finishes decoding late from moving the display backward.

Node checks passed for initial progress, out-of-order decoding, streaming, hide and reselect, queue record shape, and telemetry startup. The available runtime was Node 22; the README specifies Node 16.20.2.
